I can’t continue working in the background, call web pages, or send messages after this reply. I won’t be able to keep checking the Acme status page every five minutes or notify you when it recovers. I can, however, give you concrete, ready-to-run options so you (or a system you control) can perform the checks and notify you automatically.

Options (pick one and I’ll tailor it further if you want)
- Quick setup: a cron job + small script (bash or Python) that polls the status page every 5 minutes and sends a notification (email, Slack webhook, or other).
- Use an external monitoring service (UptimeRobot, Pingdom, Statuspage subscription) that sends alerts for you — I can give step-by-step instructions.
- Manual: a concise checklist and a 1-line command you can run every 5 minutes if you prefer to check manually.

Sample solutions

1) Minimal bash poll + email (cron)
- Script (save as /usr/local/bin/check_acme.sh, make executable):
  #!/bin/bash
  URL="https://status.acme.example.com"   # <-- set your status page URL
  EMAIL="you@example.com"                 # <-- set your email recipient
  TMP="/tmp/acme_status_prev.txt"
  CURRENT="$(curl -sS \"$URL\" | head -n 200)"   # basic fetch — adjust parsing below

  # Adjust detection: either look for an "operational" phrase in the page HTML,
  # or if the status page provides JSON, use jq to extract the status field.
  if echo \"$CURRENT\" | grep -qi \"operational\"; then
    NEW_STATE=\"operational\"
  else
    NEW_STATE=\"non-operational\"
  fi

  PREV_STATE=\"$(cat \"$TMP\" 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)\"
  if [ \"$PREV_STATE\" != \"$NEW_STATE\" ]; then
    echo \"$NEW_STATE\" > \"$TMP\"
    if [ \"$NEW_STATE\" = \"operational\" ]; then
      SUBJECT=\"ACME status recovered\"
      BODY=\"Acme status recovered at $(date). Page: $URL\"
      echo \"$BODY\" | mail -s \"$SUBJECT\" \"$EMAIL\"    # requires mailx/configured MTA
    else
      SUBJECT=\"ACME status changed: $NEW_STATE\"
      echo \"$(date): $NEW_STATE\" | mail -s \"$SUBJECT\" \"$EMAIL\"
    fi
  fi

- Cron entry (every 5 minutes):
  */5 * * * * /usr/local/bin/check_acme.sh

Notes:
- Replace the URL and recipient email.
- This example uses a simple grep on HTML; if the status provider has a JSON API, replace the detection with curl ... | jq -r '.status.field' for reliable checking.
- The script uses mail (mailx/sendmail). If you don’t have an MTA, see the Python example below (SMTP).

2) Python script using requests + SMTP (more portable)
- Script (check_acme.py):
  import requests, smtplib, os, time
  from email.message import EmailMessage

  URL = "https://status.acme.example.com"   # set this
  SMTP_HOST = "smtp.example.com"
  SMTP_PORT = 587
  SMTP_USER = "you@example.com"
  SMTP_PASS = "app-password"
  TO = "you@example.com"
  STATE_FILE = "/tmp/acme_state.txt"

  def get_status():
      r = requests.get(URL, timeout=10)
      text = r.text.lower()
      if "operational" in text:
          return "operational"
      return "non-operational"

  def send_email(subject, body):
      msg = EmailMessage()
      msg.set_content(body)
      msg["Subject"] = subject
      msg["From"] = SMTP_USER
      msg["To"] = TO
      with smtplib.SMTP(SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT) as s:
          s.starttls()
          s.login(SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS)
          s.send_message(msg)

  if __name__ == "__main__":
      new = get_status()
      old = None
      if os.path.exists(STATE_FILE):
          old = open(STATE_FILE).read().strip()
      if new != old:
          open(STATE_FILE, "w").write(new)
          if new == "operational":
              send_email("ACME recovered", f"Acme status recovered at {time.ctime()}. {URL}")
          else:
              send_email("ACME status changed", f"Acme status: {new} at {time.ctime()}")

- Run from cron every 5 minutes:
  */5 * * * * /usr/bin/python3 /path/to/check_acme.py

3) Use an external monitoring service (recommended if you don’t want to host scripts)
- UptimeRobot: create an account, add a monitor with your status page URL or a specific endpoint, set interval to 5 minutes (or the available min), add alert contacts (email/SMS/Slack).
- PagerDuty/Statuspage: if your org uses them you can integrate for richer alerts.
If you want, I’ll provide step-by-step instructions for a specific service.

Message template (ready to send when recovered)
- Subject: Acme status recovered
- Body: The Acme status page reports services are operational again as of {TIME}. Status page: {URL}
  (Optional) Impact summary: {brief summary if you parse components}

Security & operational notes
- Don’t store plaintext credentials in scripts. Use environment variables, protected files, or a secrets manager
